acceptedResidualRisks: Repository source, issue and pull request history, and intentionally uploaded sanitized artifacts are publicly readable.

The public-surface audit observed 610 Actions artifact records but did not perform a historical byte-by-byte audit; current workflows must enforce sanitization before upload and short explicit retention.

A repository administrator can still change or delete the server ruleset; post-merge hygiene exposes deletion and token-readable drift, while administrator-only drift requires a fresh owner/admin readback or another governance signal.

The ordinary ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read Ruleset bypass actors or repository security-and-analysis settings, so those administrator fields are versioned owner/admin readback evidence rather than continuously verified workflow facts.

Not storing a PAT or another long-lived administrator secret reduces credential exposure, but bypass-actor and Secret Scanning drift can remain undetected until a fresh owner/admin readback or another governance signal.
The required check context and GitHub Actions integration identity can drift and fail closed by blocking merges.
A server ruleset does not replace untrusted fork isolation, workflow token minimization, Main Provenance, or incident recovery controls.
GitHub service or API availability can block autonomous merges even when repository code is correct.
mandatoryControls: The active default-branch ruleset has no bypass actors.
Default-branch updates require a pull request, the GitHub Actions check context, linear history, and resolved review conversations.
Only squash merge is allowed; force pushes and branch deletion are blocked.
Repository merge settings disable merge commits and rebase merges in addition to the main ruleset's squash-only policy.
Pull request workflows execute untrusted fork code with read-only tokens and no repository secrets.
External-fork pull requests are never autonomously merged; token-bearing workflow_run jobs require a same-repository source.
Token-bearing provenance jobs never execute fork-controlled code.
Secret scanning and push protection remain enabled while validity checks stay disabled unless a later risk review authorizes issuer verification side effects.
The 2026-08-13 owner/admin live readback of bypass actors and security-and-analysis settings remains versioned in the Ruleset record.
Repository Hygiene continuously verifies only the subset readable by its ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN and must not claim continuous verification of administrator-only fields.
No PAT or other long-lived administrator credential is stored for continuous governance monitoring.
Probe artifacts are uploaded only after both capture and sanitization checks succeed; failure JSON is not public evidence.
Main Provenance continues to audit successful merges even though pre-receive protection is now active.
R2 and R3 changes require a current-HEAD cold-read AI review.
Secrets, real user memory, production data, private repository material, and raw chain of thought remain prohibited from commits and artifacts.
revisitTriggers: The repository becomes private again or moves to another owner.
The GitHub plan or default branch changes.
The active ruleset is disabled, deleted, bypassed, or materially modified.
Real user memory, production credentials, or production data are introduced.
More than one human collaborator receives write access.
A production release workflow is introduced.
Secret scanning or push protection is disabled.
A Ruleset, security setting, permission, or governance change affects an administrator-only field and the owner/admin readback has not been refreshed.
A PAT or other long-lived administrator credential is proposed for continuous governance monitoring.
An unauthorized direct-main update succeeds despite the active ruleset.
